findings.issue_text: packages/prisma/schema.prisma:634 — [P2, confidence 100] The new cron predicate `cancelled: true` plus `scheduledDate: { lte: ... }` has no supporting `@@index([cancelled, scheduledDate])` on `WorkflowReminder`, so every cron run scans the entire reminder table as reminder history grows.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — [P1, confidence 100] The cancellation query `where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }` omits `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`, so any cancelled SMS reminder is submitted to SendGrid with its Twilio reference and then deleted under the wrong provider contract.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:34 — [P1, confidence 75] The pre-cancellation purge `deleteMany({ where: { method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } } })` deletes a just-cancelled reminder before the following SendGrid-cancellation pass can consume it, so a queued SendGrid send that crosses its scheduled timestamp during the cron interval remains active and delivers after cancellation.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — [P2, confidence 100] `if (immediateDelete) { ... return; }` cancels the provider batch but neither deletes nor marks the rescheduled booking's persisted email reminder as `cancelled`, so rescheduling fails to complete lifecycle cleanup for already-scheduled email reminders.

packages/prisma/migrations/20230217230604_add_cancelled_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql:2 — [P1, confidence 100] `ALTER TABLE "WorkflowReminder" ADD COLUMN     "cancelled" BOOLEAN;` edits a 2023 migration that production has already recorded, so Prisma detects its changed checksum and blocks deployment before the cancelled column can be added.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — P1, confidence 100: `await client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", method: "POST", ... })` calls the newly introduced SendGrid cancellation path without any `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` in this API module, so every cancelled reminder reaches SendGrid unauthenticated and is not cancelled.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:212 — P1/100: `scheduledReminders.forEach((reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true); ... });` starts remote reminder cancellations without awaiting them, so workflow deletion returns `{ id }` after deleting the workflow while a pending SendGrid cancellation can leave the deleted workflow's email scheduled.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:573 — P1/100: `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId); ... });` is neither collected nor awaited before the mutation returns its updated workflow, so an edited workflow is reported saved while its old reminders remain active when the asynchronous cancellation has not finished.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:233 — P1/100: `catch (error) { console.log(\`Error canceling reminder with error ${error}\`); }` swallows a SendGrid cancellation failure and resolves normally, so booking reschedules and workflow changes report success while the original scheduled email is still deliverable.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — P1/75: `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request({ ... }) }` performs an unbounded series of timeout-less SendGrid requests on the cron request path, so one hung SendGrid call prevents the endpoint from completing and leaves all later cancelled reminders unsent for cancellation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:902 — The unrelated reindentation of `const hasTeamPlan = (await ctx.prisma.membership.count({ where: { userId: user.id } })) > 0;` expands a booking-lifecycle reminder change into the preview-notification authorization flow, so the next preview authorization change conflicts with this task without a behavior-related reason (P3, confidence 100; rebuttal: formatting can improve readability, but this localized deindentation neither supports the stated lifecycle objective nor applies a coherent formatting change to the file).

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

The finding correctly identifies that no index is added for this query pattern. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — [P1, confidence 100] The cancellation query `where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }` omits `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`, so any cancelled SMS reminder is submitted to SendGrid with its Twilio reference and then deleted under the wrong provider contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 44-48, the query for remindersToCancel only filters by `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate`, but does NOT filter by `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. This means SMS reminders (which use Twilio) that are marked as cancelled will also be fetched and then submitted to SendGrid's scheduled_sends API (lines 56-62) with their Twilio referenceId. This is a real bug - the query should include `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` to only process email reminders in this email-specific cron job.

adjudication.rationale: The finding references a 'deleteMany({ where: { method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } } })' operation that does not exist in the diff. Looking at the actual code in scheduleEmailReminders.ts, the query finds reminders with 'cancelled: true' and 'scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, "hour").toISOString() }', then cancels them via SendGrid API before deleting. There is no pre-cancellation purge that would delete reminders before the SendGrid cancellation can process them. The finding misreads the code flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:233 — P1/100: `catch (error) { console.log(\`Error canceling reminder with error ${error}\`); }` swallows a SendGrid cancellation failure and resolves normally, so booking reschedules and workflow changes report success while the original scheduled email is still deliverable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in emailReminderManager.ts, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function has a try-catch block that catches errors from the SendGrid API call and only logs them with console.log, then continues execution normally. This means if the SendGrid cancellation fails, the function returns successfully without throwing, so callers (like handleNewBooking.ts and bookings.tsx) will believe the reminder was cancelled when it wasn't. The original scheduled email could still be delivered. This is a real bug where error handling silently swallows failures that should propagate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — P1/75: `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request({ ... }) }` performs an unbounded series of timeout-less SendGrid requests on the cron request path, so one hung SendGrid call prevents the endpoint from completing and leaves all later cancelled reminders unsent for cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new for-loop at lines 56-66 in scheduleEmailReminders.ts that iterates over remindersToCancel and makes sequential await calls to client.request() for each reminder. There's no timeout on these SendGrid API calls, and if one request hangs, it blocks all subsequent cancellations. This is a real defect in the cron endpoint - unbounded sequential external API calls without timeouts can cause the endpoint to hang indefinitely, leaving reminders uncancelled.
